The drawing is a macrocycle with six oxygens and two benzene rings, which looks like dibenzo-18-crown-6.

**Ring atoms.** Going around the macrocycle:
- The top-left O (605,503) connects to a CH2CH2 bridge that leads to the top-right O (893,503).
- The top-right O is attached to benzene carbon (970,565) of the right-hand ring.
- The adjacent benzene carbon (1020,652) bears the right O (1037,752).
- That O connects through CH2 (1020,848) and CH2 (970,935) to the bottom-right O (893,1002).
- The bottom-right O connects through CH2CH2 (800,1033 and 700,1033) to the bottom-left O (605,1002).
- The bottom-left O is attached to benzene carbon (528,935) of the left-hand ring.
- The adjacent benzene carbon (480,848) bears the left O (461,752).
- That O connects through CH2 (480,652) and CH2 (528,565) back to the top-left O.

**Atom counts.** The ring has 6 O, 4 CH2CH2 links (8 carbons) and 4 aromatic carbons, which is 18 atoms, so it is an 18-membered crown. Each benzene is fused through two adjacent carbons.

**SMILES.** Writing it from the top-left O:
O1CCOc2ccccc2OCCOCCOc3ccccc3OCC1

Checking the order: O1, CC, O, c2ccccc2 (benzene with ortho substituents), O, CC, O, CC, O, c3ccccc3, O, CC, back to O1. The connectivity in the drawing is:
- top-left O, then CH2CH2, then top-right O, then benzene, then right O
- right O, then CH2CH2, then bottom-right O, then CH2CH2, then bottom-left O
- bottom-left O, then benzene, then left O, then CH2CH2, then back to the top-left O

This matches the SMILES.

SMILES: O1CCOc2ccccc2OCCOCCOc3ccccc3OCC1
